profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading: This building is Equinix's DC22 facility on Equinix's Ashburn, Virginia campus, part of what Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet: AOL built the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support dial-up internet operations, and the fiber infrastructure that project attracted helped trigger the region's growth into Data Center Alley in Loudoun County, now described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix established its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and DC2, which followed, has been described by Data Center Dynamics as reputedly the most connected building on earth; Equinix's own published specifications for DC2 describe a single-story, reinforced-concrete, 118,446-square-foot facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix has continued expanding the Ashburn campus well beyond DC1 and DC2, eventually building out numbered facilities into the twenties as demand grew, with Data Center Frontier reporting on Equinix's plans for a fleet of four-story buildings as part of that expansion. Equinix positions the Ashburn campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, offering colocation in private cages, smart-hands support, managed solutions, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and its own Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code but, consistent with the rest of Equinix's public site, does not publish this specific building's power capacity or square footage beyond the DC2 example cited above as representative of the campus's general specifications.

profile.regional_context: Ashburn's Data Center Alley, anchored historically by AOL's 1997 Dulles Technology Center and Equinix's own late-1990s DC1/DC2 buildings, is described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet, and Equinix's Ashburn campus serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast.

reading.body:
Equinix DC22 is a single facility within Equinix's Ashburn campus in Loudoun County, Virginia, part of Data Center Alley, the region described as holding the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. The operator does not publish DC22's power capacity, square footage, or specific certifications on its public specification page. Without published watts, the facility's scale relative to AI training infrastructure cannot be determined from the operator's own data.

Equinix does not state DC22's power capacity, so no inference about rack count or accelerator hosting is possible. The operator does publish that the Ashburn campus offers colocation in private cages, managed solutions, and interconnection products, and that it serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, qualifications consistent with a colocation facility rather than dedicated hyperscale AI training infrastructure. The campus's historical role as a peering hub and the operator's emphasis on interconnection products suggest the site's value to AI may lie primarily in network connectivity rather than in providing IT load for model training.

In Virginia, 23 of 330 mapped data center facilities publish power capacity, totaling 1,375 MW. Equinix DC22 does not publish capacity, placing it among the majority of facilities in the state for which watts cannot be verified. The published capacity across Virginia ranks 24th among all Equinix's facilities when DC22 is counted as a zero, a distinction that reflects the operator's choice not to disclose this building's specifications rather than evidence of its computational role.
